feed.title: Tesla Killed Its Solar Roof. Now Elon Musk Wants 100 GW of Solar
feed.summary: Despite recently abandoning its Solar Roof product, Tesla, under Elon Musk, is pursuing a massive solar-cell manufacturing initiative in Texas, Project Crystal Sun, aiming for 100 gigawatts of annual U.S. solar production capacity by 2028. This ambitious plan, which includes a $10.1 billion investment and thousands of jobs, comes as Musk highlights solar and batteries as crucial for meeting surging electricity demand from AI and robotics. The project signifies a shift in Tesla's solar strategy towards large-scale manufacturing rather than residential integration.

feed.title: Nykredit A S Invests $40.68 Million in Toronto Dominion Bank (The) $TD
feed.summary: Nykredit A/S has significantly increased its stake in Toronto-Dominion Bank (NYSE:TD), acquiring 334,713 shares valued at approximately $40.68 million in the second quarter. This move is part of broader institutional investment, with collective ownership reaching 52.37%. Toronto-Dominion Bank recently exceeded earnings estimates with EPS of $1.98 and revenue of $12.07 billion, and analysts maintain a "Moderate Buy" consensus with a target price of $156.

feed.title: Stellantis Canada plant's sale could allow Chinese entry, mayor warns
feed.summary: The mayor of Brampton, Ontario, warns that the sale of Stellantis's idled Brampton Assembly Plant could lead to Chinese automakers entering the Canadian market, potentially devastating the Detroit Three's business. This situation arises amid escalating trade tensions and tariffs, which have led Stellantis to shift production to the U.S. Canadian labor unions are strongly opposing the sale to a defense contractor and are pushing for Stellantis to honor its commitments and resume car assembly at the plant.

feed.title: Honda invests in US-based rare-earth-free magnet company
feed.summary: Honda Motor, through its venture capital unit Honda Xcelerator Ventures, has invested in Niron Magnetics Inc., a US-based company commercializing rare-earth-free iron nitride permanent magnets. This investment underscores Honda's confidence in Niron's technology and reflects the growing industry focus on reducing reliance on rare-earth materials, particularly from China, for high-performance magnets used in electric motors and electronics. Niron's CEO noted that the investment will support the continued commercialization and scaling of their technology across various applications, including automotive and robotics.

feed.title: This Crude Refiner Has Beaten Every Magnificent Seven Stock in the Last 2 Years
feed.summary: Valero Energy Corp. (VLO), a crude oil refiner, has significantly outperformed all Magnificent Seven stocks over the past two years, with a 203.8% rally. This performance is attributed to the widening crack spread as geopolitical disruptions have tightened both crude and refined product markets, leading to record refining margins. Despite its strong performance and earnings, the average Wall Street analyst target price for Valero is still considerably below its current trading price, though recent analyst revisions show higher targets.

feed.title: Lemonade Targets First EBITDA-Positive Quarter as CFO Tim Bixby Transitions to Board
feed.summary: Lemonade expects to achieve its first EBITDA-positive quarter in Q4, with GAAP breakeven projected roughly one year later. CFO Tim Bixby is transitioning to the board of directors after nine and a half years, with Nick Stead succeeding him, a change not expected to alter the company's strategic direction significantly. The company is focusing on growth through its technology platform, geographic and product expansion, and increased cross-selling, while balancing expansion with insurance capital requirements and aiming for long-term growth of over 30%.

feed.title: Tesla and SpaceX are fighting an Illinois company over 'Terafab'
feed.summary: Tesla, SpaceX, and SpaceXAI are suing Illinois-based tech startup Tera-print over the name "Terafab" for Elon Musk's planned massive chip manufacturing facility. Tera-print holds a trademark for "Tera-Fab" since 2017 for nanofabrication instruments and claims consumer confusion, while Musk's companies argue their uses are in vastly different commercial and technological contexts. The lawsuit, filed in Austin, seeks a declaratory judgment that Tesla and SpaceX are not infringing on the trademark, following a cease-and-desist letter from Tera-print and failed negotiations.

feed.title: Uber’s Madrid Expansion Adds a Fourth City to Its WeRide Partnership, But Its Multi-Partner Bet Faces Real Strain
feed.summary: Uber has expanded its partnership with WeRide to Madrid, making it the fourth city in their autonomous vehicle network, with plans for a commercial launch by year-end. This move aligns with Uber's strategy to rely on external AV providers rather than developing its own technology, committing over $10 billion to AV investments. However, this diversification strategy faces challenges as one major partner, Waymo, is reportedly pulling back, and another, Avride, is under a safety investigation.

feed.title: Crusoe Board Adds Cloudflare, Digital Realty, Tesla Leaders
feed.summary: Crusoe, an AI factory company, has appointed Thomas Seifert (CFO of Cloudflare), Bill Stein (Executive Managing Director and CIO of Primary Digital Infrastructure and former CEO of Digital Realty Trust), and JB Straubel (Founder and CEO of Redwood Materials and Co-Founder/former CTO of Tesla) to its board of directors. These new members bring extensive experience in energy systems, global data center networks, and scaling high-growth technology companies, which will be crucial as Crusoe expands its vertically-integrated AI infrastructure platform.

feed.title: Automaker Stocks Rally as Rotation Lifts Cyclicals: General Motors Climbs 4%, Stellantis Rises 4%, Ford Gains 3%, Tesla Adds 2%
feed.summary: Automaker stocks, including General Motors, Stellantis, Ford, and Tesla, all saw significant gains Thursday morning due to a rotation into cyclical stocks, rather than company-specific news. This movement indicates investors are betting on softer interest rates and steadier consumer confidence, driving capital towards vehicle manufacturers. However, this type of rotation-driven bid can be indifferent to individual company performance and may reverse without a fundamental catalyst.

feed.title: Tesla's Cybercab Under the Microscope: NHTSA Demands Answers to 21 Safety Questions by Month-End
feed.summary: The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) has ordered Tesla to respond to 21 detailed safety questions regarding its self-certified Cybercab robotaxi by September 30. The investigation, launched after Cybercab's commercial deployment in Austin, Texas, focuses on compliance issues including the absence of traditional driver controls, mirrors, and specific braking system requirements. This scrutiny comes amidst Tesla's push with other companies like Waymo to relax autonomous vehicle regulations, while safety advocates urge caution.

Despite a strong market position and robust demand in certain sectors, investor concerns over margin contraction, inflationary pressures, and acquisition costs have weighed on the stock. feed.title: Intel Stock Could Nearly Double to $200 in 2 Years, Analyst Says — Potential Apple, Tesla, and AI Chip De
feed.summary: Melius Research analyst Ben Reitzes predicts Intel stock could nearly double to $200 within two years, driven by potential foundry agreements with companies like Apple and Tesla, as well as strong product earnings. He highlights Intel's 14A chip manufacturing process and robust server CPU pricing as key factors. Tigress Financial Partners also maintains a Buy rating on Intel, citing its strengthening AI-focused turnaround and catalysts in data-center computing and advanced semiconductor manufacturing.

feed.title: Albemarle Q2 2026 Earnings Call Transcript
feed.summary: Albemarle reported strong Q2 2026 results with net sales up 31% to $1.7 billion and adjusted EBITDA more than doubling to $858 million, driven by higher pricing in Energy Storage and strong Specialties performance. The company raised its 2026 outlook for Specialties and expects to be at the high end of its overall guidance due to robust demand in electric vehicles and stationary storage, which has led to tight lithium markets and low inventories. Albemarle is also advancing Direct Lithium Extraction (DLE) technology at Salar de Atacama and plans further brownfield expansions at its Australian joint ventures to meet growing demand.

feed.title: Elon Musk Says 'Excitement’ is Guaranteed at Tesla Roadster Reveal in October: Audience Would Need to ‘Vouch’ That 'This Is Not AI'
feed.summary: Elon Musk has stated that the upcoming Tesla Roadster reveal on October 1st will exceed expectations, with "excitement" guaranteed, though not necessarily success. He emphasized that the audience would need to verify that the demonstration is not AI-generated, following a preview that "blew minds" according to podcast host Jason Calacanis. Musk also hinted at a possible merger between Tesla and SpaceX due to deep collaboration, which could lead to a significant payday for him.

feed.title: Nio CEO Reportedly Rules Out Buyback as Shares Hit New 52-Week Low

Li emphasized Nio's focus on sales in China and the profitability of its ES8 and ES9 models, describing the company as an energy and AI firm that is currently undervalued by the market. Nio's balance sheet, showing lower working capital compared to rivals like Li Auto, suggests the company prioritizes operational health over share repurchases.

feed.title: A $1 Billion Reason Why IBM Stock Is Up Today
feed.summary: IBM's stock rose after securing a $1 billion federal award under the CHIPS and Science Act, which will fund quantum wafer manufacturing at its spun-out company, Anderon. This funding, combined with IBM's own $1 billion commitment, validates its pivot towards deep-tech infrastructure and strengthens its position in the quantum hardware supply chain. Analysts maintain a "Moderate Buy" rating, anticipating a significant rally from current levels, making IBM an attractive investment with its strong enterprise cloud and AI performance and a 2.82% dividend yield.

feed.title: SpaceX-Tesla Merger: Ron Baron Told Elon Musk 'Whatever You Decide... Is What I'm Going to Support'
feed.summary: Billionaire investor Ron Baron, a significant shareholder in both Tesla and SpaceX, expressed his full support for Elon Musk's decision regarding a potential merger between the two companies. While he has privately discussed the pros and cons with Musk, Baron stated he would publicly back whatever choice Musk makes. Baron also highlighted the immense future value of SpaceX, particularly its Starlink unit, which he believes could generate $1 trillion in revenue within a decade.

feed.title: Will Tesla's Long-Awaited Roadster Debut With a Radical New Design?
feed.summary: Tesla is set to unveil its new Roadster on October 1, 2026, with a radical "Cyber" design and a "SpaceX package" featuring cold gas thrusters, promising a 0-60 mph time of under one second. This debut comes after significant delays and increased design ambitions since its initial concept introduction in 2017. Other auto manufacturers like Rivian and Lucid are also preparing to launch new electric SUVs, with Rivian's R2 aimed at the midsize market and Lucid's Cosmos targeting a broader customer base with a lower price point.

The company is dual-listed on the Nasdaq and Hong Kong Stock Exchange.

feed.title: First Solar To Withdraw Section 337 TOPCon Patent Case
feed.summary: First Solar has announced its intent to withdraw its Section 337 complaint with the USITC regarding TOPCon patent infringement, while retaining the option to refile later. This decision follows a new Section 232 action on polysilicon imports by the Trump Administration. The company will continue its existing TOPCon patent lawsuits in US District Court against Canadian Solar, Jinko Solar, T1 Energy, and Trina Solar, and resume global enforcement efforts.

feed.title: Morgan Stanley Backs SpaceX’s AI Potential — Expects Firm Could Help Deliver Greater Computing Power At Lower Cost
feed.summary: Morgan Stanley reiterated an 'Overweight' rating on SpaceX, highlighting its potential to enhance AI computing efficiency by expanding beyond rockets and satellite connectivity. The firm believes SpaceX's Starlink network and new AI coding platform, Cursor, could deliver greater computing power at lower costs, with Cursor potentially contributing billions to SpaceX's revenue by 2027. This comes as Starship prepares for its 14th test flight and Starlink continues to grow its aviation business, leading to an estimated valuation of $14 trillion to $15 trillion by Baron Capital CEO Ron Baron.

feed.title: Tesla must prove Cybercab is legal to sell, NHTSA says
feed.summary: The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) has issued a "special order" to Tesla, demanding that the company prove its steering-wheel- and pedal-less Cybercab is legal to sell and safe for public roads. Tesla must provide detailed information by September 30 on how the Cybercab meets federal safety standards without conventional driver controls, or face penalties. This regulatory challenge is significant for Tesla, as the company has heavily invested in its autonomous and robotaxi future.

The company's Full Self-Driving software is a key advantage, positioning it for future growth if autonomous driving regulations expand, even as its vehicle models age.

feed.title: Millions of Tesla Owners Are About to Get a Software Update That Lets The Car Intervene and Steer Even If They Never Turned on Full Self-Driving.
feed.summary: Tesla is rolling out a new software update (v14.3.9) that allows its vehicles to autonomously intervene and steer away from imminent collisions, even if the Full Self-Driving (FSD) feature was not activated by the driver. This move aims to expose more users to FSD capabilities, potentially converting them into monthly subscribers, despite Elon Musk's recent endorsement of slowing AI development, which has been flagged as a contradiction by Barron's. The company views this as a safety upgrade that also supports its monetization strategy for FSD.

feed.title: ServiceNow Stock Rises as the SaaS-Pocalypse Fear Reverses Course
feed.summary: ServiceNow (NYSE: NOW) stock is trading higher as fears of an "AI SaaS-pocalypse" recede. Originally, concerns arose that agentic AI would disrupt traditional software models by cannibalizing seat-based spending. However, recent calls from AI executives like Anthropic's Dario Amodei and OpenAI's Sam Altman for a more cautious pace of AI development are being interpreted by investors as reduced near-term disruption risk for established enterprise software platforms such as ServiceNow.

feed.title: Tesla Files to Enter Vietnam's EV Market
feed.summary: Tesla Inc. has officially entered the Vietnamese electric vehicle market by establishing a subsidiary, Tesla Motors Vietnam Limited Liability Company, in Ho Chi Minh City. The new entity, registered on September 11 with $3 million in capital, will handle wholesale and retail sales of vehicles and parts, as well as import, export, and distribution. This move signals Tesla's expansion into one of Southeast Asia's rapidly growing EV sectors.

feed.title: Gary Black Explains Tesla’s US EV Market Share Surge, Points to Legacy Retreat, Model Y Rejig: ‘It’s Implausible…’
feed.summary: Investor Gary Black attributes Tesla's dominance in the U.S. EV market to two main factors: legacy automakers scaling back their EV investments in 2025 to reduce losses, and the complete redesign of the Tesla Model Y in early 2025. He argues that Tesla's Full Self-Driving (FSD) system has not contributed to its market share gains and suggests the company should invest in marketing rather than relying on CEO Elon Musk's personal brand. Black notes that Tesla's U.S. sales are down -2% year-to-date, while overall Tesla sales are down -16% and overall U.S. EV sales are down -30% year-to-date.

feed.title: Elon Musk's Starlink Not a Threat to Wireless Carriers, Says T-Mobile CFO: ‘You Can Have a Million Satellites…’
feed.summary: T-Mobile's CFO, Pete Osvaldik, asserts that Elon Musk's Starlink is not a competitive threat to traditional wireless carriers, primarily due to fundamental physics limiting satellite-to-phone signal strength, especially indoors. While acknowledging Starlink's potential in the broadband sector for rural and suburban areas, Osvaldik criticized SpaceX's data center investment strategy as a poor allocation of capital. This comes after SpaceX's President Gwynne Shotwell announced plans to challenge telecom companies with Starlink Mobile by late 2027.

feed.title: GM Aims for Domestic Battery Supply Chain in 2-3 Years, Exec Says
feed.summary: General Motors (GM) is working to establish a domestic battery supply chain within the next two to three years, according to its VP of Battery and Sustainability, Kurt Kelty. This initiative contrasts with Ford's approach of licensing Chinese technology for battery production in the US. While GM currently imports finished battery packs from China for its most affordable EVs, it aims to develop its own domestic sodium-ion cells for stationary storage by around 2029, with similar priorities for future EV batteries.
